transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Well, occupational health at the department sent me. They're saying I'm not eating enough. 

I mean, most days I just keep it to black coffee, and then maybe a plain yogurt or a few bites of chicken at night. Honestly, sitting down for a full meal just... it feels like I'm letting my standards slip. But they wanted me to come in and talk to you about it.
Do you restrict your eating because you fear gaining weight or want to become thinner?

Yeah, I suppose it is. Look, if I step on the scale and it's up even half a pound, I get this... this jolt, like I've completely lost control of things. When that happens, I'll just spend the rest of the day cutting back even harder. I just really can't stand the idea of putting weight back on.
Has a healthcare professional told you that your current weight is significantly below what is healthy for you?

Yeah, they did. The nurse at occupational health told me my weight was dangerously low. I mean, I know my uniform hangs off me now, and I've had to tighten my duty belt past the old notches just to keep it on. But honestly, when she told me that, my first thought was still just... that I could stand to be a little sharper.
Have you had recurrent episodes where you eat an unusually large amount of food and feel unable to control your eating?

No, I don't do that. I don't really have moments where I lose control and eat a lot. Like I said, I pretty much stick to my routine with the coffee and just a little bit at night. I don't binge or anything like that.
